<reason>Both sides argued at a high level, but A built the more resilient path to victory. A's central move—forcing B to admit that caps still require an allocation rule, then showing that every "neutral" rule (lottery, open booking) still yields residents only their proportional share of global demand during the peak season the motion actually concerns—was never fully answered. B's best counter, that residents enjoy temporal flexibility across off-peak dates, was cleverly conceived but effectively neutralized in A's closing, which pointed out that the motion is specifically about peak-season access, so "try again in November" concedes rather than refutes the exclusion claim. B landed a genuinely strong revenue-math rebuttal (showing the carve-out either costs conservation revenue or, if repricing recovers it, becomes purely redistributive), and this point was left somewhat under-addressed by A's closing, which pivoted to the peak-season framing instead of squarely resolving it. But because A's core ownership/cost-bearing justification for resident priority never depended solely on the revenue argument, this gap did not collapse A's case, whereas B's temporal-flexibility answer was more central to rebutting A's "permanent exclusion" framing and it faltered under the motion's actual peak-season scope. A also offered a more concrete, workable answer to the "who counts as resident" line-drawing problem (tying eligibility to existing tax/voting/worker registers), which B never fully dismantled beyond repeated assertion. The closings crystallized this: A's was tighter and directly answered the live clash, while B's repeated its earlier framing without closing the loop on A's peak-season rebuttal.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A's pressure question forcing B to concede the cap is already binding on tourist demand, followed by B's R2 answer showing that if repricing can fully recover the discount then the carve-out is unnecessary for conservation and only serves redistribution — this was the sharpest exchange, but A's closing neutralized its force by refocusing on the motion's specific peak-season ask.</best_rebuttal>
